title: In-situ Observation of Hydrogen Interactions with Highly Strained Ni Twin Boundaries
content: Transition metal hydrides are of interest for energy storage applications and can form in other applications (e.g. catalysis) at relatively low synthetic pressure. Grain boundaries between crystalline regions contain defects and strain, which induce excess energy and reduce the enthalpy of formation of metal hydrides. Here we investigated the effect of strain distribution on the formation of Ni hydride in a Ni poly-grain film. Our in situ TEM characterization shows that Ni hydride forms at the areas with uneven strain distribution across the poly-grains with H2 flow. Ni hydride is not stable in vacuum, where the relatively fast kinetics of H transport lead to its release from the structure when there is no H2 flowing in the TEM. The strain distribution evolves during each cycle of hydride formation and stripping. These results provide insights into the structure-function relationships of transition metals for energy storage.
